classification.difficultyReason: Use the first part's exterior angle to identify the lower triangular gap, then combine its vertex angle with two heptagon interior angles around the touching point.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Consider the regular heptagon shown below. Find the angle $\theta$ indicated in the diagram.

spec.description: Regular heptagon standing on its horizontal bottom edge; baseline extends both ways and theta is outside the lower-right vertex. Decorative orange fill omitted.
spec.mathematics: Seven equal sides and angles; theta lies between the rightward baseline and the ascending side.

answer.worked:
The exterior angles sum to $360^\circ$. All seven exterior angles are equal.

$$\begin{align*}7\theta&=360^\circ\\\theta&=\frac{360^\circ}{7}.\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Consider the two regular heptagons shown below. Find the angle $\theta$ indicated in the diagram.

spec.description: Two congruent regular heptagons on one baseline, touching at their inward-facing vertices. Theta labels the upper gap. Decorative orange and cyan fills omitted.
spec.mathematics: The upper gap is between the two ascending sides at the common vertex; the lower gap is 180/7 degrees greater than the upper gap.

answer.short:
$\theta=\dfrac{180^\circ}{7}$.

Use the equal heptagon interior angles and the lower triangular gap.
answer.worked:
Each heptagon interior angle is $I=5\times\frac{180^\circ}{7}=\frac{900^\circ}{7}$. The lower gap forms a triangle with the baseline. Each base angle is $\frac{360^\circ}{7}$, so its vertex angle is $\phi=180^\circ-2(\frac{360^\circ}{7})=\frac{540^\circ}{7}$.

Angles at the touching vertex sum to $360^\circ$:

$$\begin{align*}\theta&=360^\circ-2I-\phi\\\theta&=360^\circ-\frac{1800^\circ}{7}-\frac{540^\circ}{7}\\\theta&=\frac{180^\circ}{7}.\end{align*}$$
